speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the exact nature of your left shoulder pain and how long has it been bothering you? Also, does the pain radiate anywhere else, like down your arm or into your neck?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old woman. The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of type 2 diabetes and the insidious onset of pain limiting your range of motion, does your shoulder feel stiff, particularly when trying to lift your arm out to the side or rotate it outward? Can you still actively abduct your arm beyond 90 degrees, or is the movement restricted?

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have a history of diabetes, but could you clarify if your shoulder feels specifically stiff and difficult to move, or is it primarily painful during movement? Additionally, do you have any difficulty reaching behind your back or lifting your arm above your head without assistance?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus Social history: No relevant social history provided

speaker: Doctor
text: Does your shoulder feel stiff with a true loss of both active and passive range of motion, or is the limitation only due to pain? To confirm this, I will perform a physical exam to check for "frozen" stiffness in external rotation and abduction.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your diabetes history and the reported stiffness, I suspect frozen shoulder, but I need to verify the extent of the motion loss. REQUEST TEST: Shoulder X-Ray to rule out other structural causes, and I will proceed with a physical exam to assess active versus passive range of motion.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Radiographs (AP, Scapular Y, Axillary) are Normal. Physical Examination: Shoulder shows tenderness on palpation with no warmth or crepitus. Range of Motion is significantly limited and painful: Forward Flexion 75°, Abduction 75°, External Rotation 45°, Internal Rotation 15° (significant pain). Rotator cuff strength is normal. Vital signs are stable: Temp 36.8°C, BP 130/85 mmHg, HR 82 bpm, RR 14 breaths/min.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal X-rays and the significant loss of both active and passive motion, particularly external rotation, strongly support a diagnosis of adhesive capsulitis given your diabetes history. I don't need any further tests to proceed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Adhesive Capsulitis (Frozen Shoulder)
